knowledge:
- key_parameters: min_depth=Minimum sequencing depth threshold for filtering variants (default 10) ;; filter_gd=Logical, whether to remove duplicate variants at the gene-level (default TRUE) ;; filter_pd=Logical, whether to remove duplicate variants at the positional level (default FALSE) ;; filter_vc=Logical, whether to filter variants using variant caller-specific criteria (default TRUE) ;; filter_mt=Logical, whether to remove mitochondrial variants (default TRUE) ;; filter_ns=Logical, whether to remove variants in non-standard chromosomes (default TRUE) ;; mode=In compare_profiles, 'intersection' (default) discards non-overlapping variants, while 'union' retains them ;; a, b=Parameters in calculate_similarity to weigh concordance in favor of comparisons with more overlaps (default a=1, b=5) ;; one=In compare_many, specifies a single baseline profile (e.g., COSMIC) to compare all other profiles against
- alternatives: COSMIC database (specifically CosmicCLP_MutantExport.tsv.gz or CosmicCompleteTargetedScreensMutantExport.tsv.gz) for comparing against external somatic mutation profiles instead of internal samples ;; Yu et al. (2015) 48 SNP panel, which serves as the baseline reference for the 90% cell line authenticity threshold
- when_to_use: Use when you need to authenticate cell lines or HTS samples (RNA-seq or WGS) to verify their genetic identity, or when you want to evaluate genetic similarities/differences between biological samples and characterize the biological impact of differing SNVs.
- pitfalls: Do not use the minimal subset of COSMIC files included in the package for real analyses, as results will be incomplete and inaccurate ;; If analysis of which genes or transcripts are affected by variants is desired, duplicates should be removed at the gene-level (filter_gd = TRUE) or not at all, rather than at the positional level (filter_pd = TRUE) ;; Hard thresholds for similarity are discouraged; scores just below 90% require more rigorous evaluation of specific genes/regions ;; Performing many-to-many comparisons of annotated VCF files can be computationally expensive, so saving profiles to disk using write_profile is recommended

workflows.name: snv_profile_comparison_and_similarity_analysis
workflows.intent: Create SNV profiles from VCF files, compare them to evaluate genetic similarity, and visualize the results.
input: example.vcf.gz (VCF file containing variant calls for multiple samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Create individual SNV profiles using create_profile ;; 2. Filter variants by depth or duplicates using filter_variants and filter_duplicates ;; 3. Compare profiles using compare_profiles ;; 4. Calculate similarity statistics using calculate_similarity ;; 5. Plot variant impact distributions using plot_impacts ;; 6. Perform many-to-many comparisons using compare_many ;; 7. Visualize multiple comparisons using plot_heatmap
workflows.code:
library("seqCAT")
vcf <- system.file("extdata", "example.vcf.gz", package = "seqCAT")
hct116 <- create_profile(vcf, "HCT116")
rko <- create_profile(vcf, "RKO", min_depth = 15, filter_gd = FALSE)
rko_filtered <- filter_variants(rko, min_depth = 20)
rko_deduplicated <- filter_duplicates(rko, filter_pd = TRUE)
hct116_rko <- compare_profiles(hct116, rko)
hct116_rko_union <- compare_profiles(hct116, rko, mode = "union")
similarity <- calculate_similarity(hct116_rko)
hke3 <- create_profile(vcf, "HKE3")
hct116_hke3 <- compare_profiles(hct116, hke3)
similarities <- calculate_similarity(hct116_hke3, similarity, b = 10)
impacts <- plot_impacts(hct116_rko)
profiles <- list(hct116, hke3, rko)
many <- compare_many(profiles)
heatmap <- plot_heatmap(many[[1]])

workflows.name: cosmic_database_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare sample SNV profiles against external COSMIC somatic mutation profiles to authenticate cell lines.
input: subset_CosmicCLP_MutantExport.tsv.gz (COSMIC cell line project export file)
workflows.stages: 1. List available cell lines in the COSMIC file using list_cosmic ;; 2. Read the specific COSMIC profile using read_cosmic ;; 3. Compare the sample profile to the COSMIC profile using compare_profiles ;; 4. Perform one-to-many comparisons against COSMIC using compare_many
workflows.code:
library("seqCAT")
vcf <- system.file("extdata", "example.vcf.gz", package = "seqCAT")
hct116 <- create_profile(vcf, "HCT116")
file <- system.file("extdata", "subset_CosmicCLP_MutantExport.tsv.gz", package = "seqCAT")
cell_lines <- list_cosmic(file)
cosmic <- read_cosmic(file, "HCT116")
hct116_cosmic <- compare_profiles(hct116, cosmic)
hke3 <- create_profile(vcf, "HKE3")
rko <- create_profile(vcf, "RKO", min_depth = 15, filter_gd = FALSE)
profiles <- list(hct116, hke3, rko)
many_cosmic <- compare_many(profiles, one = cosmic)

workflows.name: targeted_variant_validation
workflows.intent: Extract and visualize the genotypes of specific known variants of interest across multiple sample profiles.
workflows.stages: 1. Create a data frame of known variants with chromosome and position ;; 2. Extract genotypes for these variants across profiles using list_variants ;; 3. Format the variant list and plot the genotype grid using plot_variant_list
workflows.code:
library("seqCAT")
vcf <- system.file("extdata", "example.vcf.gz", package = "seqCAT")
hct116 <- create_profile(vcf, "HCT116")
rko <- create_profile(vcf, "RKO", min_depth = 15, filter_gd = FALSE)
known_variants <- data.frame(chr  = c(12, 12, 12, 12),
                             pos  = c(25358650, 21788465, 21797029, 25398281),
                             gene = c("LYRM5", "LDHB", "LDHB", "KRAS"),
                             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
variant_list <- list_variants(list(hct116, rko), known_variants)
row.names(variant_list) <- paste0(variant_list$chr, ":", variant_list$pos,
                                  " (", variant_list$gene, ")")
to_remove <- c("chr", "pos", "gene")
variant_list <- variant_list[, !names(variant_list) %in% to_remove]
genotype_grid <- plot_variant_list(variant_list)
